title: Cloud Organization Recon
summary: Map an organization's public cloud footprint from domains, ASN, and official pages.
objective: Build a starter inventory of cloud-related domains and services owned by a target organization.
steps: Collect official domains from website, press, and LinkedIn company page.
Run WHOIS / RDAP on primary domains and note registrar and related contacts.
Identify ASN and IP ranges via public BGP / whois services.
List subdomains from Certificate Transparency (crt.sh) and public DNS datasets.
Tag findings by likely provider (amazonaws.com, azurewebsites.net, googleusercontent.com, cloudflare, etc.).
queries: site:company.com (AWS OR Azure OR GCP OR "cloud")
companyName ("powered by" OR hosted OR cloud)
ethics: Use only public sources and authorized investigation scopes.

title: Certificate Transparency for Cloud Hosts
summary: Use Certificate Transparency logs to find cloud hostnames and SaaS endpoints.
objective: Discover hostnames that reveal cloud apps, staging, and vendor integrations.
steps: Query crt.sh for %.target-domain.com.
Export unique Common Names and SANs.
Filter names containing cloud keywords: s3, blob, storage, appspot, azure, cloudfront, vercel, netlify.
Group by environment hints: staging, dev, uat, api, admin.
Validate live hosts with passive HTTP checks only when authorized.
queries: %.example.com AND (cloudfront OR azure OR appspot OR s3)
ethics: CT data is public; active probing of systems requires authorization.

title: Public Cloud Storage OSINT
summary: Find and document publicly listed cloud storage containers using open sources — not brute force.
objective: Identify storage endpoints that are intentionally or accidentally public and record evidence responsibly.
steps: Search public indexes and search engines for storage URLs tied to the org name.
Look for official open-data portals first (government/company open datasets).
Note naming patterns from public docs: org-public, org-assets, org-media.
When a public listing is found, capture URL, listing timestamp, and sample filenames only.
Report exposure through responsible disclosure if the data appears sensitive.
queries: "index of" company (bucket OR blob OR storage)
ethics: Do not attempt unauthorized access, credential stuffing, or downloading private data. Prefer responsible disclosure.

title: GitHub Cloud Config OSINT
summary: Search public code for cloud architecture clues and accidental exposure indicators.
objective: Map cloud stack and detect possible leaked configuration patterns in public repositories.
steps: Search org/user GitHub for Terraform, CloudFormation, Bicep, Pulumi files.
Look for public references to account IDs, resource names, regions, and bucket names.
Scan for high-risk strings in public code: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, Begin Private Key, connection strings.
If secrets appear real, do not abuse them — notify the owner and revoke guidance.
Document stack choices (serverless, k8s, CDN) for investigation context.
ethics: Never use discovered credentials. Report and rotate.

title: Cloud DNS & CDN Pattern Mapping
summary: Identify cloud/CDN providers from public DNS records and CNAME chains.
objective: Determine which edge and origin providers an organization uses.
steps: Resolve NS, A/AAAA, MX, TXT, and CNAME for primary domains.
Follow CNAME chains to CloudFront, Fastly, Akamai, Azure Front Door, Cloudflare.
Record SPF/DKIM/DMARC vendors that reveal SaaS mail stacks.
Note regional hints from endpoints and TXT verification records.
Build a simple provider matrix for the case file.
ethics: Passive DNS lookups on public domains are generally acceptable; stay within scope.

title: Azure / Microsoft 365 Tenant OSINT
summary: Use public Microsoft endpoints to learn tenant and federation clues.
objective: Identify tenant name, federation status, and related domains without authenticated access.
steps: Start from known email domains of the organization.
Use public OpenID / getuserrealm style endpoints for domain realm discovery.
Note managed vs federated realm and IdP hints.
Correlate with DNS TXT verification and Autodiscover CNAMEs.
Add findings to identity topology notes.
ethics: Stick to unauthenticated public discovery methods and authorized scopes.

title: AWS Public Footprint Clues
summary: Recognize public AWS service host patterns linked to an organization.
objective: List likely AWS-hosted assets visible from open sources.
steps: Search for CloudFront distributions and S3 website endpoints mentioning the brand.
Check public JS/CSS asset URLs for s3.amazonaws.com or cloudfront.net.
Review job posts and engineering blogs for region / service mentions.
Correlate subdomain names like api, cdn, static, media with AWS patterns.
Keep an evidence table: URL, service guess, first-seen date.
ethics: No unauthorized API calls against accounts you do not own.

title: GCP Public Footprint Clues
summary: Find Google Cloud public endpoints and app hosts related to a target.
objective: Document Firebase/App Engine/Cloud Run/GCS clues from public web and CT logs.
steps: Search CT and web for appspot.com, run.app, web.app, firebaseio.com tied to brand.
Inspect public mobile/web apps for Firebase project IDs when legally obtained.
Note storage.googleapis.com links embedded in public pages.
Record project-like identifiers appearing in public JS configs.
Validate only with passive observations unless authorized.
ethics: Do not abuse Firebase/GCP APIs or bypass security rules.

title: Cloud Leak & Paste Monitoring
summary: Monitor public pastes and leak indexes for cloud credentials and asset mentions.
objective: Detect early public exposure of cloud secrets or internal hostnames.
steps: Define watch terms: legal name, domains, product names, unique bucket prefixes.
Track paste sites, public Telegram indexes, and leak alert feeds you are allowed to use.
Triage hits: false positive vs real secret pattern.
If confirmed, initiate incident response / rotation checklist.
Keep a timeline of first public sighting.
tools: Have I Been Pwned (domains you own)
ethics: Monitor brands you own or are contracted to protect.

title: SaaS & Cloud Stack Fingerprinting
summary: Identify cloud SaaS building blocks from public website signals.
objective: Produce a quick stack card: CDN, auth, hosting, analytics, support tools.
steps: Inspect public HTML/JS for vendor scripts and verification meta tags.
Check HTTP headers and cookie names on public pages.
Use public tech profilers for confirmation, not as sole evidence.
Map auth vendors (Okta, Auth0, Cognito, Azure AD B2C).
Summarize likely attack-surface categories for defensive review.
queries: site:company.com (Okta OR Auth0 OR Cloudflare OR Vercel OR Netlify)
ethics: Fingerprinting public marketing sites only unless authorized for deeper testing.

title: Wayback & Archive Cloud Asset Hunting
summary: Recover historical cloud URLs and keys references from public web archives.
objective: Find retired endpoints, old storage URLs, and leaked config remnants in archives.
steps: Query archive.org for target domains and interesting paths (/static, /assets, /config).
Download historical JS bundles that may contain old API endpoints.
Search archived text for storage host patterns.
Compare past vs present infrastructure for investigation timelines.
Store archive URLs as citations in the case file.
queries: archive.org company s3 OR cloudfront OR azurewebsites
ethics: Archives are public; still handle any sensitive remnants responsibly.

title: Cloud Incident OSINT Checklist
summary: Structured OSINT workflow when investigating a suspected cloud-related incident.
objective: Collect open-source context around a cloud incident without contaminating evidence.
steps: Define scope: org, domains, time window, incident type (leak, defacement, takeover claim).
Pull public mentions: news, social, paste, vendor status pages.
Rebuild public asset map (DNS/CT/stack) for the window.
Preserve evidence with timestamps, hashes of saved pages, and source URLs.
Separate confirmed facts vs hypotheses in the report.
queries: company (breach OR leak OR "data exposed" OR ransomware)
status.aws.amazon.com / azure status / gcp status correlation
ethics: Coordinate with lawful authority / client authorization. Do not access victim systems without permission.
